prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent (c006) combined CTS cluster_size=1/diameter=50 with allowing upper-tier BUF/CLKBUF cells. The upper-tier buffer allowance is the mechanism that generalizes (it gives rsz resources on both tiers), while the aggressive cluster_size=1 was flagged in earlier rounds as WNS-degrading. A conservative refinement: keep the upper-tier buffer allowance but restore CTS cluster_size to a moderate value (30) while keeping the reduced diameter (50), so we retain the TNS gain from upper-tier repair without the WNS loss from over-fragmented clock clustering.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.349 robust(mean-std)=+0.063 min_case=+0.065 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.189 dWNS=+8.9% dTNS=+25.8% overflow~166
  bp-ng45: score=+0.095 dWNS=+8.1% dTNS=+10.2% overflow~175
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.065 dWNS=+2.3% dTNS=+9.1% overflow~184
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: restoring CTS cluster_size=30 while keeping diameter=50 and upper-tier BUF/CLKBUF allowance yields all-valid, positive results (total +0.349, robust +0.063). All three cases improved WNS and TNS, with ariane133-ng45 strongest (dWNS +8.9%, dTNS +25.8%), consistent with upper-tier repair resources driving TNS gain without the over-fragmentation WNS penalty. Overflow ~166–184 is modest. Next step: sweep cluster_size (20/30/40) at diameter=50 to confirm 30 is near-optimal and check whether larger diameters further reduce overflow without eroding WNS.
